evidence.quote: Ccl2-/-) mice and wild-type mice with experimental peri-implantitis to evaluate the impact of CCL2 in vivo by visual examination, microcomputed tomography, hematoxylin-eosin staining, tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase staining, immunohistochemistry staining, flow cytometry, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Furthermore, using both preventive and therapeutic administration routes, the effectiveness of bindarit, which inhibited the expression of CCL2, was evaluated in experimental peri-implantitis. RESULTS: CCL2 demonstrated a significant predominant expression among the ligands of CC-chemokine receptor 2 in human peri-implantitis. CCL2 was significantly upregulated in the ligature-induced peri-implantitis model (p = 0.0007), and CCL2 deficiency resulted in significantly decreased monocytes/macrophages infiltration in peri-implant tissue (CD45+CD11b+Ly6Chi, p = 0.0019; CD45+CD11b+F4/80+, p = 0.0261), significantly reduced proinflammatory cytokine production (TNF-alpha, p = 0.0333; IL-6, p = 0.0194; IL-1beta, p = 0.0090), and significant impaired osteoclast activity (TRAP+ cells, p = 0.0240; RANKL, p = 0.0047), ultimately leading to attenuated mucosal inflammation and bone resorption in peri-implantitis.

claim.summary: In the mouse experimental peri-implantitis model, CCL2 deficiency was associated with reduced monocytes/macrophage infiltration, lower proinflammatory cytokine production, impaired osteoclast activity, and attenuated mucosal inflammation and bone resorption.
uncertainties: The evidence span is broad and includes multiple outcomes; the exact causal relation to each downstream measure is summarized rather than split into separate claims.
TRAP+ cells are mapped as a phenotype candidate; the text also lists TRAP as a gene annotation, so the molecular form is uncertain.
